# Model Variants

Also called: FWD-D, FWD-U

## Overview
This family defines three specific configurations for the forward-warping NeRF training pipeline, distinguished by their source of depth supervision and the training status of the depth estimation module. They address the problem of how to integrate depth information into the NeRF optimization loop when varying levels of prior knowledge and sensor data are available. FWD-U represents a fully unsupervised baseline, FWD introduces supervised pre-training for the depth estimator, and FWD-D bypasses the learned depth module entirely in favor of direct sensor inputs.

## Shared principles
All variants operate within the framework established by [Monocular Depth Estimation Adaptation and Supervision](12353-monocular-depth-estimation-adaptation-and-supervision.md). They utilize the volume rendering equation to compute rendered depth $\bar{D}$ and align it with an external depth source $D^*$ via local scale $w$ and shift $q$ minimization [Parent]. The core distinction lies in the definition of $D^*$ and the training dynamics of the network producing it.

## Subtopics

### FWD-U
FWD-U (Unsupervised) is the baseline variant where depth estimation is learned entirely from scratch without external supervision or pre-training. The depth estimation module, referred to as PatchmatchNet, is randomly initialized and updated end-to-end alongside the NeRF model using photometric and perceptual losses. This variant serves to demonstrate that depth can be learned implicitly through the NeRF optimization process without explicit geometric priors. It is chosen when no external depth data or pre-trained models are available, relying solely on the consistency of multi-view geometry. See [FWD-U](12354-fwd-u.md) for implementation details.

### FWD
FWD (Forward) utilizes a supervised depth estimation module that has been pre-trained using typical Multi-View Stereo (MVS) settings. The pre-trained PatchmatchNet is then fine-tuned during the end-to-end NeRF training process, updated jointly with the NeRF via photometric and perceptual losses. This variant leverages existing MVS knowledge to provide better initial depth cues, potentially accelerating convergence or improving accuracy in textureless regions compared to FWD-U. It is chosen when a pre-trained MVS model is available and one wishes to refine depth estimates jointly with novel view synthesis. See [FWD](12355-fwd.md) for implementation details.

### FWD-D
FWD-D (Direct) bypasses the learned depth estimation module entirely. Instead, it uses sensor depths (e.g., from LiDAR or structured light cameras) as direct additional inputs during both training and inference. Because sensor depths provide abundant and accurate geometry cues, no MVS module is required. This variant is chosen when high-quality sensor depth data is available, offering the most reliable geometric supervision without the error propagation inherent in learned depth estimation. See [FWD-D](12356-fwd-d.md) for implementation details.

## Background
The variants originate from the work on "FWD: Real-time Novel View Synthesis with Forward Warping and Depth" [S1]. The authors evaluated these three configurations to assess the impact of different depth accessibility levels on training and inference. The FWD and FWD-U variants were tested on ShapeNet categories, while FWD-D was designed for scenarios with direct sensor access. The distinction highlights the trade-off between the flexibility of learned depth (FWD/FWD-U) and the reliability of sensor data (FWD-D).
